app.p: Operational definition: Auditors’ questioning mindset and tendency to critically evaluate evidence, explanations, and sustainability-related claims before reaching assurance conclusions.

Measurement basis: Adapted from professional skepticism and audit judgment literature, particularly Hurtt’s professional skepticism scale and related audit skepticism studies, with contextualization to sustainability disclosures, ESG claims, and assurance evidence (Hurtt, 2010; Nelson, 2009; Nolder & Kadous, 2018; Quadackers et al., 2014).
Table A3. Measurement items for PS in sustainability assurance

td.p: When evaluating assurance evidence, I withhold conclusions until sufficient evidence has been obtained.
Adapted from general professional skepticism/evidence evaluation logic.
I require convincing evidence before accepting sustainability-related claims.
Contextualized skepticism item focused on sustainability-related claims and greenwashing risk.
I question explanations provided by clients or management when they are not supported by sufficient evidence.
Adapted from audit skepticism literature on questioning mindset and evidence sufficiency.
I pay close attention to inconsistencies between sustainability disclosures and supporting evidence.
Contextualized item targeting inconsistencies between ESG disclosure and underlying evidence.
I actively seek additional information when evaluating unfamiliar or complex sustainability disclosures.
Adapted from search-for-knowledge/questioning dimensions of skepticism and contextualized to complex sustainability disclosures.

app.p: Operational definition: Auditors’ belief in their capability to understand requirements, evaluate evidence, adapt audit skills, and perform tasks related to sustainability assurance engagements.

Measurement basis: Developed as task-specific self-efficacy items based on self-efficacy theory and general self-efficacy measurement principles, then contextualized to sustainability assurance requirements, evidence evaluation, and auditor competency development (Alamin et al., 2020; Bandura, 1977; Chen et al., 2001; International Auditing & Assurance Standards Board, 2024).
Table A4. Measurement items for SASE

td.p: I am confident that I can understand and apply relevant sustainability assurance requirements.
Task-specific capability item focused on understanding and applying sustainability assurance requirements.
I am confident that I can evaluate evidence related to sustainability information using appropriate standards and guidance.
Task-specific capability item focused on ESG evidence evaluation under relevant standards/guidance.
I can adapt my existing audit skills to sustainability assurance engagements.
Capability-transfer item linking traditional audit skills to sustainability assurance tasks.
Even when sustainability assurance tasks are complex, I believe I can perform them effectively.
Self-efficacy item reflecting confidence under task complexity.

app.p: Operational definition: Auditors’ overall favorable or unfavorable evaluation of auditors’ engagement in sustainability assurance as a professional activity.

Measurement basis: Adapted from the Theory of Planned Behavior attitude measurement logic and contextualized to sustainability assurance as an audit/professional service (Ajzen, 1991; Ajzen, 2020; Cohen & Simnett, 2015; Gipper et al., 2025).
Table A5. Measurement items for ATSA

td.p: I think auditors’ engagement in sustainability assurance is beneficial for the audit profession.
Attitude item capturing perceived benefit for the audit profession.
I have a favorable view of auditors’ involvement in sustainability assurance.
Direct favorable-evaluation item adapted from TPB attitude measurement logic.
I believe sustainability assurance is a valuable extension of traditional assurance services.
Attitude item contextualized to the expansion of traditional assurance services.
For auditors, engaging in sustainability assurance is professionally worthwhile.
Attitude item capturing perceived professional worthwhileness.

p.span: Note: ATSA = attitude toward sustainability assurance.

p.p: Intention to engage in sustainability assurance

app.p: Operational definition: Auditors’ motivational readiness, willingness, and stated plan to participate in sustainability assurance engagements when opportunities arise.

Measurement basis: Adapted from the Theory of Planned Behavior intention measurement logic and contextualized to auditing and sustainability assurance engagement settings (Ajzen, 1991; Ajzen, 2020; Alamin et al., 2020; Alleyne et al., 2013; Tuan Mansor et al., 2021).
Table A6. Measurement items for intention to IESA

td.p: I intend to participate in sustainability assurance engagements when opportunities arise.
Direct intention item adapted from Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) behavioral intention measurement logic.
I plan to seek opportunities to be involved in sustainability assurance work.
Planning-oriented intention item adapted from TPB intention logic.
I would be willing to take part in sustainability assurance engagements if such opportunities are available in my firm.
Willingness/acceptance item contextualized to firm-level engagement opportunities; revised from assigned-task wording to reduce passivity.
I intend to include sustainability assurance as part of my future professional practice.
Future professional-practice intention item contextualized to auditor role transformation.

p.span: Note: IESA = engage in sustainability assurance.
